narrative: OMX30 enters Friday with tailwind from continental Europe's strong Thursday close, particularly DAX's +1.10% momentum. Weak technical breadth—MACD below signal, RSI neutral at 55—argues for caution despite bull market regime and +4.3% cushion above 200-MA. The real driver is commodity strength: copper +1.30% and gold +0.32% directly support Boliden and industrial names, while USD/SEK's +0.43% rise benefits heavy exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson). However, ADX at 7.0 signals weak trend conviction, and OMX30 sits only -0.6% above its 50-MA—mean reversion risk is present. Geopolitical headlines (Putin/Ukraine escalation) and US yield volatility (10Y -106bps) inject uncertainty; watch for any VIX spike above 18 as a de-risking trigger.
morningBrief: OMX30 likely opens +0.3% to +0.5%, riding continental coattails and commodity momentum. Key technical level: 3123 (yesterday close) with 3085 (lower Bollinger) as support and 3180 (50-MA) as resistance. Sector rotation favours Industrials and Banks: Volvo B and Atlas Copco A benefit from USD/SEK strength and export tailwinds; SEB A and Handelsbanken A neutral to slightly positive (yields stabilizing). STRONG BUY SIGNAL: Boliden—copper +1.30% is a direct revenue driver; watch if it breaks above day's open with volume. CAUTION: Ericsson B and Hexagon B remain under pressure (NASDAQ weak, sentiment cautious). Real Estate (Balder, Castellum) should outperform given yield compression (-106bps) and risk-off tone. Monitor US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET for intraday volatility—if weak data surfaces, expect OMX30 to test 3100 support. Risk: any escalation of geopolitical tensions could spike VIX and unwind the morning's risk rally.
